context:
Goal: a simulator lease refuses only when the machine is truly busy.
Problem (rule): two of your rulings clash on how to read machine load. The simulator lease tool refuses on the load average; the load brake decision says never to use the load average.
Based on (read): bin/sim-lease lines 49-51 set MAX_5MIN=100.0, MAX_1MIN=60.0, SLOT2_5MIN=60.0; it refuses at line 180 (5-min load 100 or more, or 1-min load 60 or more) and line 189 (a second slot needs 5-min load under 60); decision sim-lease-tool (the simulator lease tool), owner-ruled.
Based on (ruling): decision machine-load-brake (when the machine is too loaded to start work), line 21: "Never the load average (107 on 15 cores while `top` showed half idle)."
Departs from: bin/sim-lease refuses on the load average — it refuses on the load brake's measure (memory in use and free disk; it reads no CPU, per your 2026-10-25 ruling).
Meanwhile: lane fixed-number-limits-census (the count of fixed limits) keeps working; nothing waits on this.

options.gain: One home for machine load; no refusal on a half-idle machine.
options.how: bin/sim-lease calls the load brake's measure and drops its three load-average numbers.
options.label: The simulator lease reads the load brake's one measure (Recommended)
options.lose: The three simulator lease numbers you set go away.

options.gain: No change to a tool that works.
options.how: The decision machine-load-brake names the simulator lease as a ruled exception.
options.label: Keep the load average for the simulator lease
options.lose: Two measures of load, one already shown wrong (107 while half idle).

ref: decision sim-lease-tool; decision machine-load-brake; lane fixed-number-limits-census
reply: Recorded 12:00 CST: the simulator lease reads the load brake's measure and drops its load-average numbers. Filed as a step for a lane.
title: Should the simulator lease read the load brake's measure of a busy machine, instead of the load average?
why: Recommended: a. Your load brake ruling already found the load average wrong on this machine, and one measure keeps one home.
